name: Agent
description: What the local agent just did — the last few things it said and changed on your desktop
author: Lattice

config.label: Entries
config.help: How many of the most recent entries to show.

config.label: Show changes
config.help: Off keeps only what the agent said, without the layout changes it made.

sections.title: What this is
items: A log of what the local agent did, newest first. It reads the same audit file the app writes, so it survives a restart.
There is no model inside this widget. It does not talk to anything and it cannot ask an agent to do something — it only shows what already happened.

sections.title: Two kinds of line
items: Plain lines are what the agent said, in its own words.
Lines with a name like placement.move are what it actually changed. Those are recorded by the app, not written by the agent, so they cannot be faked.
Reads are hidden on purpose — an agent that checks the desktop ten times would otherwise bury the one thing it changed.

sections.title: If it stays empty
items: Agent access is off. Turn it on in Settings → Agent access; nothing can connect until you do.
Or nothing has connected yet. The board fills the first time an agent asks for something.
The widget also needs the Agent activity permission. Without it the card says so instead of pretending to be empty.

sections.title: Why it asks for a permission
items: This list is your history: what was moved, when, and what the agent said about it. A widget that can read it and also reach the network could send it somewhere.
Grant it only to widgets you trust with that.

changes: First release: shows what the agent said and changed, newest first.
Refreshes on the platform scheduler, so a hidden card costs nothing.
